DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

They Cried in 1955

STS-HS11-L4-1400P-HSVPAMA1112-TTM-LAT-01 • HS Media Arts 11–12 • Intent, Meaning, and Reception of Media Artworks
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Your mission: travel back to March 1955, to a movie palace on Broadway in Los Angeles. In those years, theaters there showed films from Mexico's Golden Age of cinema to packed crowds of Mexican American families, and many people in the seats lived far from the towns where they grew up. A song about a faraway home could bring a whole row to tears. When Paloma's class watched the same scene this week, most of them laughed.
Why would the same scene make one audience cry and another audience laugh?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Paloma doing?
Look at the picture. Build a reasoned spoken answer about Paloma's action, grounded in visible evidence, and close by explaining what her work contributes to the class's study of audience reception.
2
What is Emiliano holding?
Look at the picture. Build a reasoned spoken answer about what Emiliano holds, and evaluate why it is stronger evidence of the 1955 audience than a guess would be.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Build a reasoned spoken answer about the teacher's action, and explain why showing the same scene again is central to this mission.
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Build a reasoned spoken answer about this place, weigh the competing details, and explain why this setting suits a mission about 1955 audiences.
5
Tell me about the audience board.
Look at the picture. Build a reasoned spoken answer about the board, and argue why one scene could produce opposite reactions from audiences in different times and cultural contexts.
6
What is Renata wearing?
Look at the picture. Build a reasoned spoken answer about Renata's clothing, and explain how the students' costumes support the mission's purpose.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
